papers.title: Lifting connectivity bottlenecks in superconducting quantum processors via enriched native two-qubit gates
papers.abstract: Limited qubit connectivity is a central architectural constraint in superconducting quantum processors, whose planar layouts require additional gates to mediate interactions between distant qubits. Here, we use the AshN control scheme, where rich two-qubit control on every nearest-neighbour pair allows a logical interaction and the required qubit routing to be merged into a single native operation, effectively transforming a sparse hardware graph into a more connected computational architecture. For the benchmark instances studied, the resulting synthesis capability enables reliable execution on constrained one- and two-dimensional lattices, with compiled two-qubit gate counts approaching those of an all-to-all-connected reference. Across seven benchmark circuits on one- and two-dimensional topologies, the AshN-based implementation achieves geometric-mean reductions of $45.2\%$ and $43.7\%$ in two-qubit gate count compared with controlled-Z-based compilation, respectively. Using AshN gates, we prepare an eight-qubit two-excitation Dicke state with a fidelity of $0.736$ and certify its genuine multipartite entanglement using a fully positive-partial-transpose witness, whereas the same witness does not certify entanglement for the CZ-based implementation. The state fidelity and entanglement certification remain robust across the tested lattice configurations, including those with up to three connectivity defects. Our work establishes native-gate engineering as a practical approach to mitigating connectivity constraints.

summary.summary: The paper demonstrates that enriched native two-qubit control via the AshN scheme—combining tunable coupling with simultaneous microwave drives—enables SWAP absorption into adjacent gates, effectively increasing the connectivity of superconducting qubit processors with fixed coupling graphs. On benchmark circuits with 1D and 2D topologies, AshN compilation achieves 45.2% and 43.7% reductions in two-qubit gate count compared to controlled-Z, with experimental validation on an 8-qubit Dicke state achieving 0.736 fidelity and certified genuine multipartite entanglement even under connectivity defects.
summary.motivation: Planar superconducting processors face routing bottlenecks due to sparse connectivity, requiring extra SWAP gates to implement distant interactions. This work addresses whether richer native gate sets can mitigate connectivity constraints without adding physical couplers, by exploiting closure properties under SWAP composition.
summary.method: The authors calibrated AshN gates across a 12-qubit 1D chain and 3×3 2D array using parallel calibration procedures that exploit characteristic Hamiltonian dynamics, implemented SWAP-aware MirrorSABRE routing to absorb SWAP operations into adjacent two-qubit blocks, and benchmarked the resulting circuits against controlled-Z implementations on seven circuits, larger compilation instances, and Dicke-state preparation under connectivity defects.
summary.result: For structured application circuits, two-qubit gate count overhead relative to all-to-all connectivity decreased from 1.65× (CZ) to 1.13× (AshN) on 2D lattices, and the 8-qubit Dicke state fidelity improved from 0.631±0.001 (CZ) to 0.736±0.001 (AshN), with the AshN implementation certifying genuine multipartite entanglement across defective topologies where CZ-based implementations failed.

papers.title: Bang-bang protocol for nondispersive qubit readout
papers.abstract: Fast, precise, and quantum-non-demolition (QND) readout of superconducting qubits is a fundamental component of high-fidelity quantum sensing and computation. Conventional approaches typically operate in the dispersive regime, where the qubit-resonator coupling $g$ is weak compared to the detuning $Δ$. While exhibiting good QND properties, the readout rate is limited to $\sim g^2\sqrt{N}/Δ\ll g$, where $N$ is the number of photons in the resonator. QND readout in the nondispersive regime, where the readout rate reaches its full potential $\sim g$, relies on parameter sweeps that may encounter resonances, leading to measurement-induced state transitions (MIST). In this work, we study a nondispersive readout protocol that replaces these sweeps by sudden quenches of the coupling constant, using a resonator that is preloaded with photons. We call this protocol bang-bang readout, and show that it realizes single-shot projective measurements. The fidelity and QNDness of the qubit post-measurement are remarkably high, with an error that decreases like $1/N$. To arrive at these findings, we develop an analytical theory for the dynamics and measurements of the Jaynes-Cummings (JC) model, including a systematic expansion of correction terms in powers of $1/\sqrt{N}$. We show that the protocol can also be implemented without preloading the resonator by instead strongly driving the qubit, e.g., with a classical flux drive.

Realizing Rapid, High-Fidelity, Single-Shot Dispersive Readout of Superconducting Qubits

summary.summary: This paper presents a bang-bang protocol for nondispersive qubit readout using sudden quenches of the qubit-resonator coupling instead of adiabatic parameter sweeps. The protocol achieves fast, high-fidelity quantum-non-demolition readout with errors scaling as $1/N_\mathrm{eff}$ by exploiting dynamics in the Jaynes-Cummings model with a large photon number $N_\mathrm{eff}$.
summary.motivation: Conventional dispersive readout limits the readout rate to $\sim g^2\sqrt{N}/\Delta \ll g$, while adiabatic approaches in the nondispersive regime ($g^2 N/\Delta^2 \gg 1$) encounter measurement-induced state transitions from multiphoton resonances. Eliminating parameter sweeps via sudden coupling quenches offers a route to fast, QND readout without these resonance crossings.
summary.method: The authors develop an analytical theory for the Jaynes-Cummings model combining saddle-point approximation with systematic perturbation theory in $1/N_\mathrm{eff}$. A preloaded resonator couples suddenly to the qubit at strength $g$, pointer states separate at rate $g$ over readout time $t_r \approx 4g^{-1}$, then the coupling switches off for projective resonator measurement. The qubit post-measurement occupies time-dependent sweet-spot states $|\pm(t)\rangle$ with high purity.
summary.result: At typical parameters ($g/2\pi \approx 100$ MHz, $\Delta/2\pi \approx 23$ MHz), readout times drop below 10 ns with QNDness and fidelity exceeding 99% at effective photon number $N_\mathrm{eff} \geq 11$, representing $>10\times$ speedup over dispersive readout while maintaining high-fidelity state preservation for mid-circuit measurements and reset.
